$comment: Voice-over, captions and animation for the demo video. After recording, set each cue's "at" (m:ss in the RAW recording) to the moment its event appears on screen, then run scripts/demo/demo.ps1 edit. A cue with "at": null is skipped. *Starred words* are highlighted in the caption. "badge" shows a section label (top-left) and a title for 2 s. "zoom": [centreX, centreY, factor, seconds], centres as fractions of the screen; the defaults assume the run-sheet layout (Moon panel on the right, terminal at the bottom). Check them in the check/ images and adjust. Put your own recording of a line in <voice-dir>/<id>.wav to use your voice.

cues.text: Moon is a VS Code coding agent whose agent loop runs on *TrueForge*. This is Flask 3.1.3.
First, cancellation. I start an inline edit and press *Stop* while text is streaming.
The preview is gone at once, and git status shows *no changed files*.
Task A. I select get_debug_flag, press Control I, and paste the exact instruction.
The reply *streams* from TrueForge events, and the editor stays usable.
The diff is drawn inside the file, with *Accept and Reject on every hunk*. I accept each hunk on its own.
With FLASK_DEBUG set to off, get_debug_flag now prints *False*.
I restore the file so the next task starts from clean code.
Task B, agent mode. The request *names no files*.
A *scout subagent* picked these files. The context card shows each file, why it was chosen, and the project map's *token budget*.
Each tool call is one line in the log. The agent edits a *hidden copy* of the project, not my files.
Running pytest needs my approval. This card is a *TrueForge tool approval*.
apply_changes is an approval tool too, and it opens the review. The change spans *code, tests and docs*, files the agent found itself.
I accept the hunks and press Apply. *Only accepted hunks* reach the disk.
The CLI tests *pass*, flask help lists the new command, and secret values print as *three stars*.
The same run in TrueForge: the turns, the *MCP tool calls*, and the *scout subagent*.
*Undo this whole run* puts every file back. git status is clean again.
Task C. The main Claude provider now has an *invalid key* in TrueForge.
I repeat Task A with the same instruction.
Claude fails with a *401*, and Moon switches to the backup model, *DeepSeek on Azure*, with no click from me.
The editor keeps *responding* while the backup works.
The backup's diff is here, and git status shows *no changed files*.
Moon. It orbits your code and *lands only when you say yes*.
